summary.text: Scott Martin is a Republican who has represented Pennsylvania's 13th Senatorial District in Lancaster and Berks Counties since being elected in November 2016 (re-elected in 2020 and 2024), and chairs the Senate Appropriations Committee.

paragraphs.text: Before the Senate, Martin was a Lancaster County commissioner, a licensed realtor and landlord, and for 13 years worked in the juvenile justice system, including as director of the Lancaster County Youth Intervention Center. His biography says that as commissioner he never voted for a tax increase and reduced county debt by $40 million.

He graduated from Lancaster Catholic High School, where he was a PIAA and national heavyweight wrestling champion, and from Millersville University with a degree in sociology and criminal justice, where he played football.

In the Senate he previously chaired the Education and Local Government committees. His biography credits him with a constitutional amendment approved by voters in May 2021 limiting a governor's open-ended emergency declarations, and with bills creating the Grow PA grant program and the Safe2Say Something school threat reporting system.
He chairs the PA Athletic Oversight Committee, was elected chair of the Chesapeake Bay Commission in 2023, and he and his wife Amber have four children.
